
  The deeper lesson of terminal multiplexers is architectural. They demonstrate
  the power of inserting a small, stable layer between two things that change at
  different speeds: the ephemeral terminal in front of you and the long-lived
  work you care about. That separation — presentation from process, viewer from
  state — is the same principle behind detachable containers and remote
  development servers. It is telling that a design from 1987 remains not just
  relevant but newly useful in 2026. Fashions in developer tooling churn
  constantly, but the problem of keeping work alive while windows come and go is
  permanent, and the multiplexer's answer to it has aged remarkably well.

  ---

  a different tone, more technical depth on tmux specifics, a shorter or longer
  version, or a different structure? I'll wait for your reply.
